$comment: The one list the /buchen/ page shows: the formats. What was needed on
site and the frequently asked questions used to stand here too, and
stood on the page under the cards; both are gone. Prose lives in
sections/*.php as it does everywhere — only what repeats or grows
lives here. The values themselves are website content and stay German.
!!! NOTE: the formats are DRAFTS. The durations, what the cards say and
the occasions they name are guesses and have to be reviewed by you.
While "reviewed": false stands here, `make check` points it out.
"occasions": the kind of evening this format is usually booked for —
a list, because it grows and shrinks as we learn what people ask for,
and because it is the one part of a card somebody scans rather than
reads. It stands at the foot of the card, under the rule and over the
button, as one line with dots between the words: they are their own
label, and the rule already says the description has ended. Leave the
list out or empty and the foot holds nothing but its button.
Two formats, and that is the whole menu: what somebody booking an
evening decides is whether they want to watch or to play. How long a
show runs is a line in the card, not a format of its own — the short
appearance and the full evening used to stand here as two entries,
which made the difference between them look like the choice.
How many there are is not written down anywhere else: the heading over
the cards counts them (sections/booking-formats.php). A third entry
here therefore says "Drei Formate" by itself.
Prices deliberately appear nowhere: "on request" is more honest than a
number that then turns out to be wrong. As soon as you want to name a
range, it goes in here as "price" per format.

formats.name: Bühnenshow
formats.summary: Wir spielen, euer Publikum gibt die Ideen.
formats.detail: Schnelle Spielformen aus Zurufen aus dem Saal, vereinzelt können auch Zuschauer auf die Bühne, wenn sie wollen. Im Ganzen ein runder und entspannter Abend für alle.

formats.name: Impro zum Mitmachen
formats.detail: Warm-ups, einfache Spielformen, bei denen jeder mitmachen kann. Ideal geeignet für Teams, Geburtstage und sonstige Anlässe, um gemeinsam eine einzigartige Erfahrung zu erleben. Vorerfahrung braucht niemand.
